vignette: A 72-year-old hypertensive man has sudden weakness of the left arm and leg with ataxia of the same limbs out of proportion to the weakness; sensation, speech and vision are normal.
stem: Which structure best explains the combination?

options.text: Right posterior limb of the internal capsule with corticopontine fibers

explanation: Ataxic hemiparesis is a lacune of the posterior limb (or basis pontis) interrupting the corticospinal tract and the corticopontine fibers together; the corticopontine input crosses in the pons and the cerebellar output crosses back, so ataxia lands on the weak side. A cerebellar lesion would give ipsilateral ataxia without weakness.
